Edit this 2D game character sprite sheet. It is a texture atlas for a 2D skeletal animation (Spine) character: a chibi Chinese warrior in a long robe, drawn as 15 separate pieces packed on a transparent background - head, back hair, front hair pieces, warrior cap, hair knot, body robe, left arm, right arm, right hand, left foot, right foot, and three robe drape panels (left, right, back).

Change the character into a young girl and change the outfit into traditional Chinese Hanfu.

Convert each piece, keeping its exact silhouette, size, rotation and position:
- head: same size, same facing direction and same pose, but a young girl's face - soft feminine features, no beard, thin eyebrows, small calm eyes, same skin tone, same brushwork.
- back hair: long flowing female black hair, same footprint and same length.
- front hair pieces: female front hair locks and side bangs, same shapes and same placement.
- warrior cap: replace it with a traditional Chinese female hair ornament, a hairpin with hanging beads, occupying exactly the same footprint and the same silhouette weight.
- hair knot: a silk hair ribbon, same shape and same size.
- body robe: Hanfu cross-collar robe, flowing silk, same silhouette and same shoulder width.
- arms: Hanfu wide sleeves, same pose, same length, same volume.
- hand: small delicate hand, same footprint.
- robe drape panels (left, right, back): Hanfu skirt and sleeve drape panels with the same silhouette, same outline and same size as the originals.
- feet: embroidered cloth shoes, same shape and same size.

Keep absolutely unchanged: the layout of the sheet - every piece stays in the same position, same rotation, same canvas footprint, same scale and same spacing from the others; the transparent background with no new background, no shadow and no ground; the number of pieces - exactly 15 separate pieces; the art style, line quality, brushwork, shading and painterly texture; the chibi proportions of every piece; the original colour palette, only shifted toward soft feminine Hanfu tones.

Do not draw a full character as one connected silhouette. Do not connect the arms to the body or the hair to the head. Do not merge any two pieces. Do not add or delete pieces. Do not add text, labels, watermark, UI, borders or a frame. Do not change the canvas size or the aspect ratio. Do not add faces or details to pieces that have none.

nodes.title: Note: settings
widgets_values:
## Qwen-Image-2.1 edit - Hanfu atlas

This graph is the official template flattened: no subgraph,
so every node is directly visible/editable.

**Sampler** (do NOT use classic img2img values here)
- denoise: 1 - the model is an instruction-edit model.
  Edit strength comes from the *prompt*, not from denoise.
- cfg: 1 - keep it. The negative prompt is only read when cfg > 1.
- euler / simple / 25 steps here (official pipeline uses 40-50, slower).

**resolution** (widget on the TextEncode node)
- total pixel budget, aspect ratio of image_1 is preserved.
- 0 = keep the reference size (253x142) - far too small here.
- 1024 is a pixel BUDGET, not a side. The canvas is snapped to
  a multiple of 32 and keeps image_1 aspect. This asset
  (253x142) at 1024 gave 1376x768 = ~1.06 MP. Measured, not
  guessed. This machine has 15.9 GB VRAM and the weights alone
  are ~15.8 GB, so do NOT raise this to 2048.
- Upscale the result back down to 253x142 (or rescale the atlas)
  so the existing 1113103_1.atlas coordinates stay valid.

**image_1** = edit target (the atlas page).
**image_2** = optional style reference; its LoadImage is muted.
Unmute it, upload a file and it is read from `<image2>`
in the prompt. Address refs as <image1>, <image2>, ...
